samples.summary: `review` still instructs the user to `cd scripts/agent && npm ci` for the SDK, but the panel now runs out of the pipeline checkout where Node will never resolve `scripts/agent/node_modules`.
samples.evidence: The token gate at line 303-310 warns "run `claude setup-token` … and `cd scripts/agent && npm ci`", then line 350-361 spawns `node <clone>/packages/pipeline/review-panel.mjs`. Node resolves the bare `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` specifier (imported lazily inside `ask.mjs`) by walking up from the IMPORTING file, i.e. `<clone>/packages/pipeline/node_modules`, `<clone>/node_modules`, … — it never reaches this repo's `scripts/agent/node_modules`. So a user who follows the printed instructions builds the diff, spawns the panel, and gets ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND from `fail("local review panel failed: …")`. The guidance should name the pipeline checkout as the place to install.

samples.summary: `pipelineDir` treats a valueless `--pipeline-dir` as absent, so a mistyped invocation silently skips the review instead of failing — contradicting the rule stated three lines below it.
samples.evidence: `parseArgs` (line 157) sets `a[key] = true` when a flag has no following value, and `pipelineDir` does `typeof args["pipeline-dir"] === "string" ? … : env.AGENT_PIPELINE_DIR`. So `spec-to-pr.mjs review --pipeline-dir` (or `--pipeline-dir --dry-run`) falls through to the env var and then to `return null` → the "skipping the local review panel — no pipeline checkout" warning, having been explicitly asked to use one. The comment at line 145-146 states the intended principle for exactly this class of mistake ("a typo, not a missing option — say so rather than silently falling through to the skip path"); `args["pipeline-dir"] === true` should reach `fail` too.

samples.summary: In the verify path `assertClosed` exits before the collected `problems` are printed, so a deleted vendored module is reported as "the vendored set is not closed" instead of the accurate "missing: vendor/pipeline/<f>".
samples.evidence: Line 175-179 accumulates `missing:`/`EDITED:` entries into `problems`; line 181 then calls `assertClosed(VENDOR, onDisk.filter(...))`, which `die`s (process.exit(1)) on the first unresolved import; the `if (problems.length)` report is at line 183. Because `assertClosed` is fed `onDisk` (what is present) rather than `listed`, a module deleted from `vendor/pipeline/` makes every sibling's import of it "not closed", and the operator is told to "Add the missing module to FILES … and re-run --write" when the real fault is a locally removed file. Moving the `problems` report above `assertClosed`, or checking closure against `listed`, gives the accurate diagnosis.

samples.summary: `reappearedMirrorFiles` compares full relative paths, so a pipeline file re-added under any subdirectory of `scripts/agent/` is not detected as the mirror growing back.
samples.evidence: `walk(root).filter((f) => pipelineFiles.has(f))` — `walk` returns paths like `foo/severity.mjs` while `pipelineFiles` holds `severity.mjs`, so the membership test misses it. The job's stated contract (ci.yml:296, "no pipeline file may reappear here") and the die message ("The pipeline mirror is growing back in scripts/agent/") both claim more than the check performs. Note the test at scripts/test/verify-pipeline-drift.test.mjs relies on this same full-path comparison as one of the two reasons `vendor/pipeline/severity.mjs` is not reported, so tightening it to a basename match would need the `vendor/` STAYS exclusion to carry that case alone.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. verify-pipeline-drift.mjs derives all evidence from IMPORT_RE matches (line 36/142) and filename set-membership (line 126); nothing inspects string paths, and main() prints the unconditional success line at 234 and exits 0. All three cited references are dangling in this tree: scripts/agent/lenses/** is empty (harvest.mjs:66, cache-report.mjs:248) and the only review-panel.mjs files are vendor/pipeline/ and the CI-created .trusted/ copy, so eval/run.mjs:81's DEFAULT_PANEL_SCRIPT resolves nowhere and is used unconditionally at run.mjs:754 — eval-replay.yml only passes --panel-script on a dry run (lines 367-372), so a real paid replay spawns a missing script. cache-report.mjs:248 reaches loadLenses (vendor/pipeline/review-panel.mjs:2365), a bare readFileSync that throws ENOENT with no --lenses-dir. The job is blocking (ci.yml:301-352, no continue-on-error) and its comment at 345-351 claims exactly the protection it does not provide. I searched for a counterexample check and found none: verify-self.mjs LANES, verify-ci.mjs, vendor-pipeline.mjs (hash manifest only), scripts/test/* (incl. the drift test, which only covers import-shaped cases at 121/186), eslint.config.mjs, and the agent suites contain no path-existence assertion. Partial mitigation only: harvest.mjs:2042-2048 wraps its read in try/catch, so that instance degrades (panelSaw empty) rather than crashing — the other two remain unguarded, so the finding stands.
